narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`deft session:start` (mutation, not `--read-only`) prints `fatal: not a git repository` twice, then continues and exits 0. The line comes from a recoverable probe against the npm-installed framework root, which is not a Git checkout.

This is additional dogfood on #3914. #3914 reproduces the same fatal on `deft session:start --read-only` at v0.108.0 and names the managed-AGENTS framework-SHA probe. This filing records that the same stderr still ships on mutation `session:start` at v0.110.0.

## Observed on

- Consumer: `deftai/statusreport`
- Engine: `@deftai/directive@0.110.0` (npm, `managed_by: npm`)
- Host: Grok Build, Windows, PowerShell
- Date: 2026-09-02
- Command: `deft session:start` (mutation; host also injected `--session-id=host:claude:v1:...`)

## Actual output (prefix)

```
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
[deft ceremony-dial] depth=rapid ...
Deft Directive active -- AGENTS.md loaded.
USER.md resolved (platform-config): ...
[deft scm] SCM ready: ghx present, host-gh authenticated (shallow)
...
occupancy claimed session host:claude:v1:... (intent=mutation)
[deft] session ritual recorded at ...
```

Exit code 0. Ceremony completed. The consumer repo **is** a Git repository (`C:\Repos\deft\statusreport`). The probe that fails is against the installed `.deft/core/` / package tree.

The fatal printed twice on every `session:start` in this session, including after the 0.110.0 deposit refresh.

## Expected

- A successful `session:start` does not print a raw Git fatal for a recoverable framework-SHA probe.
- An actual SCM failure stays visible.

## Related

- #3914 — same fatal; currently scoped around read-only syntax plus suppressing that probe stderr. Please treat this as recurrence / widening evidence (mutation start, two lines, 0.110.0), not a second root cause unless investigation splits it.
- Another consumer agent hit the same mutation-start fatal in a parallel session and will comment here with their reproduction.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Mutation `deft session:start` in a Git consumer with an npm `.deft/core/` deposit emits no `fatal: not a git repository` line on success.
- [ ] The same holds for `deft session:start --read-only` (#3914).
- [ ] Actionable Git/SCM failures still print stderr.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-02T18:53:50Z)

model: claude-sonnet-5
role: critic

Round 1 critic, refutation charter, N=1 spend. Id ceiling 5514603456 (the triage write-back, the only comment on this thread at dispatch). Dispatch SHA `9b78332de5e328874a470d78994499d1d29446f5` (confirmed via `git rev-parse HEAD` in the dispatched worktree). Process-only pass: I audit the recorded premise, protocol fit, and recording obligations, and I do not implement.

All line cites below were re-read against the worktree at the dispatch SHA. The child-process behavior in F1 and F2 was executed in a controlled fixture (temp directory, no `.git` ancestor), not merely read.

## Re-verification of the refutation-target

The recorded target — "mutation `session:start` still prints raw `fatal: not a git repository` from a recoverable framework-SHA probe against the npm-installed framework root, then continues and exits 0" — survives. `resolveFrameworkSha` in `packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts:69-83` is unchanged from the shape #3914's arc diagnosed: `execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--short=12", "HEAD"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8", timeout: 5000 })` with no `stdio` override, wrapped in a `try/catch` that swallows the exception and returns `"unknown"`. #3914's bound synthesis (comment 5502221319, citing successor lean 5502150939) accepted this as real and not yet fixed; nothing in this repo's tree between that arc and this dispatch SHA touches the function. The premise is confirmed true, not merely re-asserted.

## Inventory of existing mechanisms

- `defaultGitRunner` (`packages/core/src/session/git.ts:28-58`) — genuinely silent: `stdio: ["ignore","pipe","pipe"]`, captures stderr into a return value instead of letting it reach the parent's stderr.
- `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` (`packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts:85-98`) — the "own-git-root" gate #3914's synthesis names as already in tree.
- `resolveFrameworkSha` (`platform/agents-md.ts:69-83`) — the leaking probe itself, called from two independent sites in a cold mutation `session:start`: `resolveHostContentSurface` → `host-content-surface.ts:184`'s direct `agentsRefreshPlan(...)` call (session-start.ts:1429, and also at :866/:960 on the read-only/re-arm paths), and `runOrientationCompression` → `runAgentsRefreshOrientationSection` (`orientation-compression.ts:314-388`, invoked at session-start.ts:1577) → `applyAgentsRefresh` → `agentsRefreshPlan`.
- The duplicate resolver `packages/core/src/doctor/agents-md.ts:45-64` uses `spawnSync` with no `stdio` override either, but that call is only reached from `eval/health.ts`, not from `session-start.ts`; it does not contribute to this bug's console output (spawnSync's own default does not inherit stderr the way execFileSync's does — confirmed the asymmetry empirically, not asserted).

## Findings

### F1 — `blocks-the-design`: the second "already in tree" mechanism is not actually silent

Evidence, executed: a Node fixture reproducing `payloadIsOwnGitRoot`'s exact body (`execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse","--show-toplevel"], { cwd, encoding: "utf8", timeout: 10000 })`, no `stdio` override) against a directory with no git ancestor prints `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` to the real process stderr, then returns `false`, exit 0 — the identical leak-then-recover shape #3914 diagnosed in `resolveFrameworkSha`. `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` itself never routes through `defaultGitRunner`.

Failure mode: #3914's accepted synthesis (5502221319) states "the existing own-git-root check and the silent git-runner already in tree are the mechanisms, not a new probe." A build that reads that literally — gate `resolveFrameworkSha` on `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` and call it done — moves the leak rather than closing it: on the exact deposit shape #4118 reproduces (frameworkRoot with no git ancestor at all), the gate call itself prints the raw fatal before the SHA probe ever runs. Both #3914's and #4118's acceptance criteria ("emits no fatal... line on success") would still fail after that literal reading.

Disposition consequence: this does not reopen or recut #3914's binding — #4118's own refutation-target is untouched. It blocks treating "wire the two existing mechanisms together" as sufficient off-the-shelf: whoever implements the fix must also route `payloadIsOwnGitRoot`'s own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` through a silent runner (`defaultGitRunner` or equivalent captured-stdio), not only gate the SHA probe behind it as currently implemented.

Road not taken / steelman: the alternative reading is that #3914's "already in tree" phrasing was accurate as written and #4118 needs no further scoping beyond re-running the bound design. Rejected because that reading is contradicted by an executed fixture against the named function, not by a plausible-sounding alternative — `payloadIsOwnGitRoot`'s source has no silent-runner indirection to point to.

### F2 — `sharpens-framing`: two independent call sites explain the "twice," and explain why read-only differs

Evidence, executed: running the fixture from the re-verification section twice in one process (simulating `resolveHostContentSurface`'s drift-check call and `runAgentsRefreshOrientationSection`'s apply call, both against a directory with no git ancestor) prints the fatal line twice, with two independent `"unknown"` returns and a clean exit — reproducing #4118's transcript exactly (two consecutive fatal lines before any deft output, then normal completion).

Failure mode without this: a reviewer could read "prints twice" as unexplained or nondeterministic, or a narrow fix could patch one call site (e.g., only `applyAgentsRefresh`'s internal call) and leave `host-content-surface.ts:184`'s separate direct `agentsRefreshPlan` call untouched, silencing mutation start down to one fatal line while still failing both AC items and still leaking on `--read-only` (which only exercises the `host-content-surface` call site).

Disposition consequence: the target does not change, but its scope sharpens — fixing the shared `resolveFrameworkSha` (plus F1) closes both call sites at once, because both routes bottom out in the same `agentsRefreshPlan` → `resolveSha` chain in one file. This also grounds the triage's "widening, not a second root cause" framing mechanically rather than by assertion: read-only fires one of the two call sites (`resolveHostContentSurface` only), mutation fires both.

### F3 — footnote: this filing evidences one half of #3914's two-part finding, not the other

#3914's arc found two distinct defects in the SHA probe: (a) the stderr leak on a directory with no git ancestor (the "not a git repository" text), and (b) a non-checkout nested *under* an unrelated ancestor repo silently returning that ancestor's SHA (gpt-5, comment 5502134138). #4118's transcript text ("not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git") matches (a) exactly and does not exercise (b). This filing is fresh evidence for the leak half only; it says nothing new about the wrong-SHA-ancestor half, which stays exactly as scoped in #3914's existing binding.

## Injection / swarm lens

Not triggered: the target is a local child-process stderr leak in a session-start probe. It does not change authority, untrusted input, prompts/envelopes, identity, concurrency, worktrees, or shared state.

## Protocol fit

Stop 1 write-back (5514603456) is well-formed: `mechanism-shaped: true` plus the mirrored `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` label are both present on the issue; `refutation-target:` names one premise, not a conjunction; `charter`/`spend` are recorded as two separate fields; `sha:` matches this dispatch's `git rev-parse HEAD` exactly; `related:` cites #3914's actual synthesis comment id, and that citation checks out against the fetched comment. No recording-obligation defect found.
